PolicyMismatch chargesShort MWhExcess MWhHours coveredCapped orders

Planned quantity is capped at 4 MWh per zone-hour and 120 MWh per delivery day across both zones. Within each daily batch, all DK1 hours receive capacity before DK2 hours; hours are ordered within each zone. This prioritizes DK1 when the shared limit binds.

Method, cost accounting and limitations
  • Sources: Energinet gross consumption and day-ahead prices. Gross consumption includes transmission losses. Quarter-hour prices are averaged; incomplete hours are not filled.
  • Training ends 31 May. Validation runs 15 June–14 July. Calibration runs 28 July–17 August. Testing runs 1–29 September. Gaps allow the 12-day label delay. No coefficients, model choices or residual offsets are refitted on the test period.
  • The source reports initial, preliminary and final data. Preliminary values typically have an 8–10-day delay; final revisions can occur much later. A 12-day allowance is a conservative modeling assumption, not proof that archived values were known then.
  • Point candidates are the two-week seasonal forecast, mean of corresponding hours 2–4 weeks earlier, and ridge regression with penalties 1, 10 and 100. Validation selects independently by zone. The simplest model is retained when it wins.
  • Q50/Q80/Q90 plans add the corresponding empirical quantile of signed calibration residuals to the point forecast, floored at zero. A separate absolute-residual, finite-sample split-calibration radius forms the nominal 90% interval. Time dependence and drift can invalidate its coverage assumptions.
  • For assumed shortage charge Cs and surplus charge Co, the unconstrained cost-minimizing quantile is Cs/(Cs+Co). Constant residual offsets approximate the conditional quantile; volume constraints can change the optimal joint plan.
  • Cost = actual MWh × spot price + max(actual−accepted, 0) × Cs + max(accepted−actual, 0) × Co. This assumes shortages bought at spot+Cs and excess sold at spot−Co. These are synthetic charges, not actual balancing rules or quotes.
  • All policies serve the same actual load; the spot-cost component is common. No liquidity, transaction fees, collateral, credit risk, actual customer data, weather forecasts or tariff structure are modeled.
  • Orders move PROPOSED → APPROVED → OPEN → SETTLED. A rejected order becomes REJECTED_RECONCILED after its uncovered load is accounted for. Caps, a kill switch, duplicate protection, chronological events and delayed reconciliation are implemented.
  • The saved SQLite book is Q80 at €200/€50 charges. The report also simulates Q50/Q90 and alternative charges. The 90% interval and Q90 service target are different quantities and need not have the same observed coverage.
